newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Body of suspected Arab collaborator discovered.
newsitem.headline: Body of suspected Arab collaborator discovered.

text.p: Israeli troops discovered near the West Bank city of Nablus on Saturday the body of a Palestinian suspected of collaborating with Israel, officials said.
Nablus governor Mahmoud al-Aloul said the Palestinian Authority was investigating the killing.

"The body of a Palestinian who holds an Israeli identification card -- the kind Israel gives to collaborators to protect them -- was found east of Nablus in an area outside the security control of the Palestinian Authority," Aloul told Reuters.
"We are investigating the case," he said.
An Israeli police spokesman said soldiers discovered the body while on patrol near Nablus. He said the man had been tortured and shot in the head.
"The body was taken to the forensics institute for an autopsy," the spokesman said.
Palestinians have killed scores of fellow-Arabs suspected of collaborating with Israel and several have been detained by PLO police.
Israeli authorities have allowed many collaborators to take up residence in Israel since it transferred control of parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip to the PLO in 1994.
